new writes an issue folder, generates an id nothing else in the repository
is using, and puts it on a report/<id> branch for a pull request.

The id is a hash of the issue's own fields and eight bytes of randomness, so
allocating one needs no counter, no lock and nobody's agreement — which is the
only thing that works when half the issues in flight are on branches nobody has
pushed yet. It is regenerated if it collides with any id isu can see.

--no-branch writes into the working tree and commits nothing, which is what a
bulk conversion needs.

Usage:
  isu new [flags]

Flags:
      --acceptance string    what done looks like (required on a story)
      --blocked-by strings   issues this one waits on
      --body string          the markdown below the frontmatter
  -h, --help                 help for new
      --no-branch            write into the working tree instead of onto a report branch
      --owner string         the human answerable for it (default: git's user.name)
      --parent string        the epic this belongs to
      --priority string      p0, p1, p2 or p3 (default "p2")
      --question string      what is being answered (required on a spike)
      --repro string         how to reproduce it (required on a bug)
      --title string         one line saying what this is (required)
      --type string          bug, story, chore, spike or epic (default "bug")

Global Flags:
      --fetch         update remote refs before reading
      --json          print newline-delimited JSON instead of text
      --no-color      never colour the output
      --ref string    the ref isu treats as trunk (default: main, else master, else HEAD)
      --repo string   the repository to read (default: the working directory)
